title: Predicted hurricane transitions split NHC 48-hour circle coverage but gave no clear added score gain in two basins in 2017-2025
abstract: We tested whether predicted hurricane-strength transitions add track uncertainty information beyond initial forecast wind. Earlier-year four-cell radii split initial and verifying-time forecast wind at 64 kt. In 2017-2025, 48-hour proper quantile loss changed by -1.84% in the Atlantic (95% storm limits -3.74 to +0.30%) and +0.05% in the eastern Pacific (-1.14 to +1.24%). Thus neither primary storm interval shows a clear gain. Weak-start Atlantic reference coverage differed by 19.26 percentage points between forecasts that did and did not reach hurricane strength. A future-observed wind diagnostic also gave uncertain score gains. We recovered 122 verifying winds missing from the eastern Pacific error table at its 140 W boundary with a matching HURDAT2 snapshot. All 76 checked archived 48-hour forecast winds matched exactly. Revised source records, binary groups, fixed-fit intervals, stage exclusions and prior archive inspection limit inference. The package includes original code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and independent arithmetic checks.

display.caption: Added loss change from initial-wind radii. Forecast-wind and future-observed-wind rules have primary storm intervals that include zero.
